- When sentiment is low (≤0.2) and forecast is high, reduce forecast by 1–2% to avoid overreaction.  
- If recent price spike (last 3–5 days) is followed by forecast overshoot, cap forecast at +10% above recent peak.  
- If sentiment is high (≥0.4) and forecast is low, adjust upward by 0.5–1.5% to reflect bullish momentum.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome is consistently 1–2% below forecast, apply downward bias correction by 0.5–1.0% in next forecast.  
- If sentiment history shows strong negative sentiment (e.g., 0.0–0.1) and forecast is rising, reduce forecast slope to avoid false optimism.  
- Mean-reversion bias: if forecast is 3–5% above recent 7-day average, reduce by 0.5–1.0% unless sentiment supports continuation.  
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome is >10% above forecast, check if sentiment was high — if so, consider model underestimating bullish sentiment.
